name: Manching

attributes.attribute: a Continental Celtic archaeological site, one of the largest Celtic settlements excavated near Ingolstadt
surrounded by a five-mile-long wall and rich in domestic and ritual artifacts
recorded by Koch as an oppidum where a late La Tène vessel inscribed BOIOS was found

text: Manching was a Continental Celtic archaeological site. Excavators uncovered a Celtic settlement near the Bavarian town of Ingolstadt. A wall five miles long surrounded the buildings of the settlement. Archaeologists found domestic and some ritual artifacts there. Most of them are in museums in Munich and Ingolstadt, with some kept at a small museum on the site. Koch records a late La Tène vessel bearing the inscription BOIOS, a Boian, dating to the first century B.C., found in the oppidum of Manching. The find connects the settlement to the Boii, the Celtic people who gave their name to Bohemia.
objective: Document Manching, the great Continental Celtic settlement and oppidum near Ingolstadt.
